L2732@P64: RESEARCH ON THE TECHNOLOGY OF HYPERSPECTRAL REMOTE SENSING OIL-GAS EXPLORATION BASED
L2733@P64: ON VEGETATION REFLECTION SPECTRUM ANOMALIES
L2734@P64: Li Qianqian , Chen Xiaomei, Liu Na, Ni Guoqiang and Lan Tian
L2735@P64: School of Optoelectronics, Beijing Institute of Technology, Beijing, China
L2736@P64: Key Laboratory of Optoelectronic Imaging Technology and System, Ministry of Education, Beijing, China
L2737@P64: Abstract : Seepage of underground oil-gas reservoirs will bring stress effects for poisoning of roots of vegetation in the
L2738@P64: environment, which will be reflected in vegetation canopy reflectance spectra. In order to explore how to extract anomalous vegetation resulting from natural oil-gas microseepage by hyperspectral remote sensing images, this paper presents a data processing
L2739@P64: flow for effectively extracting wild anomalous vegetation resulting from oil-gas microseepage. Sparse vegetation covered area
L2740@P64: in Yulin, China was taken as an experimental zone, the CASI images were used as test data, wild vegetation anomaly spectrum
L2741@P64: information resulting from oil-gas microseepage was extracted according to the flow, and the oil-gas anomaly zone is hereby delineated. Locations of small gas wells known in the research zone and the resulting anomaly zone are highly conforming, which
L2742@P64: verifies the effectiveness of the data processing flow, and can provide some reference and basis for oil-gas exploration in other
L2743@P64: cover type areas.
L2744@P64: MAPPING ECOSYSTEM SERVICES USING IMAGING SPECTROSCOPY DATA
L2745@P64: Daniela D.M. Braun, Alexander Damm, Rogier de Jong, Michael E. Schaepman,
L2746@P64: Remote Sensing Laboratories, Geography Department, University of Zürich – Irchel, Winterthurerstr. 190, CH-8057, Switzerland
L2747@P64: Abstract : Ecosystem services (ES) generate benefits to human well-being but quality and amount of their provisioning
L2748@P64: is threatened by environmental change. Remote sensing techniques allow assessments of ES at critical scales using combinations
L2749@P64: of remotely measurable ecosystem properties. In this contribution, we use an ES assessement approach suggested by Homolová et
L2750@P64: al. and extend it to estimate ES supply continuously for a heterogenous landscape across different Earth spheres using data of the
L2751@P64: Airborne Prism Experiment (APEX) imaging spectrometer. We further suggest a conceptional framework to combine ES maps
L2752@P64: to match the needs of different stakeholders. Our results show the heterogenuous supply of agronomic ES, carbon sequestration
L2753@P64: and cultural ES within the landscape and and its different ecosystems. Our proposed ES mapping approach and the conceptual
L2754@P64: framework developed for combining ES according to stakeholder requests, provide spatially explicit information on ES across
L2755@P64: heterogeneous landscapes and can therefore improve decision-making of stakeholders.
L2756@P64: EVALUATION OF BREFCOR BRDF EFFECTS CORRECTION FOR HYSPEX, CASI, AND APEX IMAGING SPECTROSCOPY DATA
L2757@P64: Daniel Schläpfer, ReSe Applications Langeggweg 3, 9500 Wil, Switzerland
L2758@P64: Rudolf Richter, German Aerospace Center (DLR) DE-82234 Wessling, Germany
L2759@P64: Abstract : The correction of BRDF effects for airborne wide FOV imaging spectroscopy data is of interest for a consistent
L2760@P64: data processing and products generation. Recently, a new BRDF effects correction method (BREFCOR) has been implemented
L2761@P64: as additional processing step after the well-known atmospheric compensation workflow. This paper shows validation results of
L2762@P64: the method for sample data sets of HYSPEX, CASI, and APEX data. It can be shown that the method is able to deal with a broad
L2763@P64: variety of sensors and surface characteristics. The quality of the spectral albedo data products is substantially increased in terms of
L2764@P64: consistency for all data sets. Future potential improvements and additions for a better operational usability and for the processing
L2765@P64: of complete spectra are finally summarized.
